title: Early Voting Is Open: What Every Webb County Voter Needs to Know, Starting Today

content:
Polls opened this morning. Early voting for Laredo’s November 3 municipal election runs from today, October 19, through Friday, October 30. If you live in Webb County and plan to vote, this is your window.

When and where

According to the Webb County Elections Office’s published schedules:

  • Mon, Oct 19 – Fri, Oct 23: 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
  • Sat, Oct 24: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
  • Sun, Oct 25: 12 p.m. to 6 p.m.
  • Mon, Oct 26 – Fri, Oct 30: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

The county operates 14 early-voting locations. The main site is the Webb County Elections Office, 720 Convent Ave. in Laredo. Permanent branch locations include the Barbara Fasken Recreation Center (15201 Cerralvo Dr.), the Laredo Fire Department Administrative Center (616 E. Del Mar Blvd.), the City Hall Annex (1102 Bob Bullock Loop), and the McKendrick/Ochoa/Salinas Library (2901 Palo Blanco St.), plus nine temporary branches countywide. Full location lists and sample ballots are available on the county’s elections pages.

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Webb County uses countywide vote centers, meaning on Election Day you may vote at any of 39 locations — not just your home precinct. The deadline to apply for a ballot by mail is Friday, October 23.

What’s on the ballot

Voters will choose the mayor — incumbent Dr. Victor Treviño faces JD Gonzalez, Alfonso “Poncho” Casso, Alyssa Cigarroa, and Jorge A. Garza — plus city council representatives for Districts I, II, III, and VI, and the judge for Municipal Court Place 1. Beyond city hall, TX-28 voters decide between Rep. Henry Cuellar and Webb County Judge Tano Tijerina for Congress. Our full bilingual ballot guide covers every race beyond the headline contests.

Why this window matters

Turnout in Laredo’s municipal elections has historically been low, and early voting is where most of those votes are cast. The city launched its nonpartisan “Laredo Votes 2026” campaign in September — information, not endorsement — with a focus on neighborhoods where participation lags. Registration for this election closed October 5, so if you’re registered, the only question left is when.

Two and a half weeks of early voting, 14 locations, evening and weekend hours. The watchdog’s note: a ballot you don’t cast is a decision you let someone else make for you.
